decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP

geo.name: GEO

govern.name: Governance

stories.head: Salesforce launches Koa reasoning model trained on decades of CRM data
stories.plain: Salesforce is embedding a purpose-built reasoning model called Koa into its platform, trained on its own CRM history to handle operational customer-interaction work. This matters because it signals a shift from general-purpose LLMs to domain-specific AI — changing how enterprise buyers evaluate and purchase marketing AI.

stories.head: ChatGPT Ads are a tactical test, not a platform strategy, MarTech argues
stories.plain: An analysis urges marketers to treat ChatGPT's new ad inventory as a low-cost experiment while keeping Google spend intact. With Adform confirmed as a launch partner in Europe (article 19), this is a real buying decision landing on desks now — making the strategic framing directly actionable for media planners.

stories.head: Adform becomes OpenAI technology partner as ChatGPT Ads expand into Europe
stories.plain: OpenAI's ad product is now live in Europe via certified platform partners like Adform, giving marketers a concrete buying route into AI-native ad placements inside ChatGPT. Early adoption signals and a named DSP integration mean this is no longer hypothetical — it changes the channel mix discussion today.

stories.head: 3 techniques to add governance guardrails to AI-driven PPC accounts
stories.plain: Optmyzr lays out concrete automation-layering methods that let teams keep human oversight while running AI bidding and targeting in live accounts. Practical guardrails for agentic ad tools are still rare, so a clear how-to directly affects how AI is built and governed inside paid-media stacks.

stories.head: Martech strategy must start with the operating environment, not the tools
stories.plain: This piece argues that informal institutional knowledge — how things actually get done — is now being exposed and disrupted by AI, forcing teams to rethink martech strategy from the ground up. It reframes how organisations should approach AI adoption decisions, making it relevant to anyone buying or governing marketing technology.

stories.head: Salesforce's Koa reasoning model bets CRM history beats generic AI
stories.plain: Salesforce is embedding decades of CRM data into a reasoning model called Koa designed to handle operational tasks behind customer interactions. This matters because it signals a competitive strategy where proprietary training data — not just model size — becomes the main differentiator in how enterprise marketing AI is bought and evaluated.

stories.head: ChatGPT Ads are a tactical bet, not a platform strategy
stories.plain: A MarTech analysis argues marketers have a short window to test cheap ChatGPT ad inventory before prices rise, but warns against shifting core budget away from Google. Combined with Adform's European ChatGPT Ads rollout, this reframes how AI-native ad surfaces should enter a media plan — as experiments, not foundations.

stories.head: Who owns your AI agents after they launch? Governance gap explored
stories.plain: This piece tackles a growing blind spot: once an AI agent is deployed, no team clearly owns its maintenance, oversight, or shutdown. It offers a framework for assigning accountability across marketing, IT, and legal. As agentic systems proliferate in MarTech stacks, this governance gap is becoming a real operational and legal risk.

stories.head: IAB: AI-driven media discovery is outpacing marketers' ability to measure it
stories.plain: IAB data shows ad budgets rising into AI-mediated channels while measurement frameworks lag badly behind. Marketers can't yet reliably track how AI-driven discovery influences the customer journey. This is a structural buying problem — money is moving before the ROI tools exist to justify or optimise those moves.

stories.head: Can you see what informs your marketing agent's recommendations?
stories.plain: Sponsored by Rokt mParticle, this piece makes a practical case that agentic marketing only works if marketers can inspect the underlying data driving agent decisions. It connects CDP data quality directly to agent trustworthiness — a concrete argument for why governance and data infrastructure must precede agentic deployment.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Need Owners, Not Just Launchers
body: Marketers are deploying AI agents into live ad accounts, CRM workflows, and customer journeys — but governance frameworks have not kept pace. The question of who is accountable for an agent's decisions after go-live is becoming a board-level risk, not just an IT footnote.

Optmyzr's advice on making AI safer in live ad accounts and Rokt mParticle's push for recommendation transparency both signal the same underlying demand: visibility and control must be designed in from the start, or teams will be auditing damage rather than optimizing performance.
ev: MarTech · 3 ways to make AI safer

themes.head: ChatGPT Ads: Tactical Bet vs. Platform Strategy
body: OpenAI's ad product is arriving in Europe with Adform as a launch partner, triggering immediate budget experimentation. But analysts are warning that buying impressions inside an AI assistant is a media tactic, not a substitute for building a presence in AI-driven discovery more broadly.

The deeper strategic question — who controls the digital storefront when conversational AI becomes the default search interface — is reshaping how CMOs think about organic reach, paid placement, and brand authority simultaneously. Early movers are treating ChatGPT Ads as a test-and-learn line item while protecting investment in owned channels.

themes.head: Brand Consistency Breaks Under AI Scale
body: AI content generation is exposing gaps that human teams papered over: only 14% of shoppers currently experience a consistent brand, according to Athos Commerce research. When AI systems execute at speed, ambiguous brand guidelines produce visibly inconsistent outputs across every channel simultaneously rather than gradually.

The fix is not more rules documents — it is structured brand logic that AI can actually parse. Teams that invest now in machine-readable brand standards will compound that advantage as generation volume grows; those that don't will spend budget on correction rather than creation.
ev: MarTech · AI scales promises faster than trust

themes.head: CRM Data as the Moat for Enterprise AI
body: Salesforce is explicitly framing decades of CRM data as its competitive differentiator against pure-play AI vendors — a bet that proprietary customer context beats generic model capability. The concurrent expansion with Bandwidth into a native global contact center underlines how the platform is weaving AI into every customer touchpoint it already owns.

This matters for buyers: the vendor selection question is shifting from 'which AI model is best?' to 'which platform holds the richest longitudinal data about my customers?' Enterprises already deep in a CRM ecosystem face rising switching costs, making data portability and interoperability non-negotiable evaluation criteria.
ev: MarTech Series · Bandwidth & Salesforce contact center
MarTech · Real CMO AI decision this quarter

themes.head: AI Is Outrunning Measurement — and the Org Chart
body: AI is reshaping media performance faster than attribution models can track it, and the confusion is cascading into organizational restructuring: marketing teams keep redrawing their org charts precisely because no one is sure where AI decision-making sits relative to human roles. Mediaocean launching an AI ventures fund and Flam closing a $40M Series B show capital is still flowing in, but operational clarity is lagging.

The in-house model is under particular stress — AI is compelling some brands to bring more capability inside while simultaneously making external specialist platforms more powerful. The teams winning are those that define their operating environment first, then choose tools; those that stack tools first are discovering the strategy gap mid-execution.

month.takeaway: Across every signal this month, the common thread is that AI is executing faster than the strategies, governance structures, and measurement systems built to guide it — and the marketers who close that gap first will define the next competitive baseline.
